items.title: XAI2Brain: A Perspective on Mechanistic Interpretability for Brain–AI Alignment
items.summary: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), explainable AI (XAI), and neuroscience is fostering new opportunities for understanding both machine and biological intelligence through interpretable and human-centered learning paradigms. In this Perspective, we introduce XAI2Brain as a conceptual framework for brain–AI alignment, positioning mechanistic interpretability as an intermediate layer connecting neural network representations, human understanding, and neuroscience-inspired AI design. items.title: RDoC-informed explainable AI as a paradigm for multilevel Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis and progression prediction: a systematic review
items.summary: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is gaining popularity in early diagnosis and monitoring of dementia. items.title: The causal efficacy of consciousness: a neuroscientific analysis and explanation
items.summary: This study analyzes neural and behavioral events occurring before, during, and after the emergence of a pain quale and the consciousness of that pain to examine the causal efficacy of the quale and consciousness. It finds that events occurring before or concurrently with the emergence of the quale are neither caused nor influenced by the quale or consciousness. items.title: Defining spinal motor neuron subtypes across development: from embryonic specification to postnatal maturation
items.summary: Spinal motor neurons are essential for translating neural activity into coordinated muscle contraction, yet defining their functional subtypes across development remains a persistent challenge. While embryonic patterning establishes the initial positional and molecular framework of motor neuron identity, substantial refinement continues during early postnatal life as intrinsic electrophysiological properties, synaptic connectivity, and neuromuscular interactions mature. items.title: The Neuroscience of Metaphor as Abstraction
items.summary: Metaphor has been suggested to be one of the pinnacles of human cognition, yet the neural underpinnings of figurative language is hotly debated and findings are often controversial. The goal of the present paper is to demonstrate that the available neuroscientific evidence on metaphor opens a window on an essential core of human language. Contrary to the widely shared assumptions of embodied cognition, metaphor reveals the fundamentally abstract functioning of the language system in its pristine form. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. items.title: Image processing with ImageJ
items.summary: Wayne Rasband of NIH has created ImageJ, an open source Java-written program that is now at version 1.31 and is used for many imaging applications, including those that that span the gamut from skin analysis to neuroscience.
